subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A nurse teaches a client with left-leg weakness how to use a cane. On which side should the client hold the cane?

options.feedback: Correct. The cane is held on the stronger side and advances with the weak leg.
Incorrect. Holding it on the weak side does not offload the affected leg.

options.text: In whichever hand feels more comfortable
options.feedback: Incorrect. Placement is based on the weak leg, not comfort.

options.text: In front of the body with both hands
options.feedback: Incorrect. A cane is a single-hand device.

rationale: A cane is held on the stronger side to provide support to the weaker leg.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: How often should a nurse reposition a bedbound client to help prevent pressure injuries?

options.feedback: Correct. Repositioning every 2 hours relieves pressure over bony prominences.
Incorrect. This is far too infrequent to prevent tissue breakdown.

options.text: Only when the client requests it
options.feedback: Incorrect. Repositioning must be scheduled, not client-initiated.
Incorrect. Prolonged pressure causes ischemia within a couple of hours.

rationale: The standard is to reposition an immobile client at least every 2 hours.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A client is receiving a continuous enteral tube feeding. To reduce the risk of aspiration, how should the nurse position the client?

options.text: Head of bed elevated at least 30 degrees
options.feedback: Correct. Elevating the head of the bed reduces reflux and aspiration risk.
Incorrect. Lying flat increases the risk of reflux and aspiration.
Incorrect. This does not address vertical reflux risk during feeding.
Incorrect. Head-down positioning increases aspiration risk.

rationale: Keeping the head of the bed elevated 30-45 degrees during and after feeding prevents aspiration.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: Which item should the nurse include when calculating a client's fluid intake?

options.feedback: Correct. Gelatin is liquid at body temperature and counts as intake.
Incorrect. Solid food is not counted as fluid intake.
Incorrect. Solid food is not measured as fluid.
Incorrect. Solid protein is not counted as fluid intake.

rationale: Foods that are liquid at room or body temperature (gelatin, ice cream, broth) count toward fluid intake.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A nurse must assess pain in a nonverbal client with advanced dementia. Which tool is most appropriate?

options.text: A behavioral pain scale that observes facial expression and body movements
options.feedback: Correct. Observational/behavioral scales are used when a client cannot self-report.
Incorrect. This requires the client to verbally rate pain.

options.text: Asking the family to rate the pain from memory
options.feedback: Incorrect. Direct observation of the client is more valid.

options.text: Waiting until the client can speak
options.feedback: Incorrect. Pain assessment should not be delayed.

rationale: For nonverbal clients, behavioral/observational pain scales assessing facial and body cues are appropriate.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: While providing postmortem care, which action should the nurse take first after the client is pronounced dead?

options.text: Provide privacy and allow the family time with the body if they wish
options.feedback: Correct. Supporting the grieving family with privacy is a priority in postmortem care.

options.text: Immediately remove all tubes without checking policy
options.feedback: Incorrect. Removal depends on facility policy and any medical examiner involvement.
Incorrect. The body is placed supine in normal alignment.
Incorrect. Belongings are gathered and given to the family.

rationale: Postmortem care includes providing privacy and family support along with respectful body preparation per policy.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A nurse performs passive range-of-motion exercises for an immobile client. What is the primary purpose of these exercises?

options.text: To maintain joint mobility and prevent contractures
options.feedback: Correct. Passive ROM preserves joint flexibility when the client cannot move independently.
Incorrect. Passive ROM does not significantly increase muscle mass.

options.text: To increase the client's heart rate for exercise
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is not the goal of passive ROM.

options.text: To replace the need for repositioning
options.feedback: Incorrect. ROM does not replace pressure-relief repositioning.

rationale: Passive ROM maintains joint range and prevents contractures in clients who cannot move their joints actively.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A client reports constipation. Which nonpharmacologic measure should the nurse recommend first?

options.text: Increase dietary fiber and fluid intake
options.feedback: Correct. Fiber and fluids are first-line nonpharmacologic measures for constipation.
Incorrect. Routine enemas are not a first-line measure.
Incorrect. Activity promotes peristalsis and helps relieve constipation.

options.text: Limit fluid intake to reduce bloating
options.feedback: Incorrect. Reducing fluids worsens constipation.

rationale: Increasing fiber, fluids, and activity are first-line nonpharmacologic interventions for constipation.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A client with a newly applied plaster cast asks how to relieve itching under the cast. What should the nurse advise?

options.text: Direct cool air from a hair dryer set on the cool setting into the cast
options.feedback: Correct. Cool air relieves itching without breaking the skin.

options.text: Insert a knitting needle to scratch the skin
options.feedback: Incorrect. Inserting objects can injure skin and cause infection.

options.text: Pour lotion down inside the cast
options.feedback: Incorrect. Moisture and lotion under a cast promote skin breakdown.

options.text: Remove padding at the cast edge to scratch
options.feedback: Incorrect. Altering the cast is unsafe.

rationale: Cool air relieves itching under a cast safely; inserting objects risks skin injury and infection.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A client reports difficulty falling asleep in the hospital. Which nonpharmacologic action should the nurse take first?

options.text: Reduce noise and dim the lights during the night
options.feedback: Correct. Promoting a quiet, dark environment supports sleep.
Incorrect. Caffeine is a stimulant that interferes with sleep.

options.text: Schedule vital signs every hour through the night
options.feedback: Incorrect. Frequent interruptions worsen sleep.
Incorrect. Long daytime naps can disrupt nighttime sleep.

rationale: Reducing environmental stimulation is a first-line nonpharmacologic sleep-promotion measure.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: A postoperative client has not voided for 8 hours and reports lower abdominal fullness. Which nonpharmacologic action should the nurse try first to promote voiding?

options.text: Run warm water over the perineum or turn on a running faucet
options.feedback: Correct. Sensory cues such as warm water and running water stimulate voiding.
Incorrect. Catheterization is not the first step; try noninvasive measures first.
Incorrect. Restricting fluids does not promote voiding.

options.text: Place the client flat and tell them to hold it
options.feedback: Incorrect. This does not relieve retention.

rationale: Noninvasive measures such as warm water and the sound of running water stimulate voiding before catheterization.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: While assisting a client with a bed bath, which action best preserves the client's dignity?

options.text: Keep the client covered, exposing only the area being washed
options.feedback: Correct. Draping and exposing only one area preserves dignity and warmth.

options.text: Leave the door open to save time
options.feedback: Incorrect. An open door violates privacy.

options.text: Fully uncover the client for the entire bath
options.feedback: Incorrect. Full exposure is unnecessary and undignified.

options.text: Discuss the client's care loudly with a passing coworker
options.feedback: Incorrect. This breaches privacy and confidentiality.

rationale: Draping the client and exposing only the area being washed maintains dignity, privacy, and warmth.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: Which measures help prevent pressure injuries in an immobile client? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep the skin clean and dry
Massage vigorously over reddened bony prominences
Keep the client in one position to avoid disturbing them
Ensure adequate protein and fluid intake

rationale: Repositioning, clean dry skin, pressure-redistributing surfaces, and good nutrition prevent pressure injuries; massaging reddened areas is contraindicated.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: Which are nonpharmacologic measures a nurse can use for pain relief? Select all that apply.
rationale: Heat/cold, imagery, positioning, and massage are nonpharmacologic; opioids and IV rate changes are not.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: Which nursing actions are appropriate when administering an enteral tube feeding? Select all that apply.

options.text: Elevate the head of the bed at least 30 degrees
Flush the tube with water per protocol
Hang formula that has been at room temperature for 24 hours
Check gastric residual per facility policy
Administer the feeding rapidly by gravity bolus in under a minute

rationale: Verifying placement, elevating the head, flushing, and checking residuals are safe practices; expired formula and rapid infusion are not.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: Which findings suggest that a client may have poor nutritional status? Select all that apply.
rationale: Weight loss, poor healing, brittle hair/nails, and muscle wasting indicate poor nutrition; good turgor and stable appetite are normal.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: Which instructions are correct when teaching a client to use a standard walker? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep all four legs of the walker on the floor before stepping
Move the walker forward a short distance, then step to it
Lean far over the front of the walker when walking
Keep the elbows slightly flexed while gripping the handles
Use the walker to climb stairs like a step stool

rationale: Stable four-point contact, short advances, nonskid shoes, and slight elbow flexion are correct; leaning over the walker and using it on stairs are unsafe.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: Which 3 sources should the nurse include when measuring a client's fluid output?
rationale: Output includes urine, emesis, and liquid stool; oral and IV fluids are intake, and solid food is not measured.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: Nonblanchable redness over the sacrum in an immobile client is an early sign of a stage 1 pressure injury.
rationale: Persistent, nonblanchable erythema over a bony prominence indicates a stage 1 pressure injury.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: The most reliable indicator of a client's pain is the nurse's judgment of how much pain the client should be feeling.
rationale: The client's self-report is the most reliable indicator of pain, not the nurse's judgment.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: For each item, click to specify whether it is recorded as intake or output on the fluid balance record.
rationale: Fluids taken in (juice, gelatin, IV) are intake; urine and emesis are output.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: For each comfort or ADL measure, select all goals it helps achieve (may support more than one).
rationale: Repositioning and dry, smooth linens both comfort the client and protect skin; massage and warmth mainly promote comfort.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: Before administering an intermittent tube feeding, the nurse should first {1}, and to reduce aspiration risk should keep the head of the bed elevated to at least {2}.

choices.text: clamp the tube for an hour

rationale: Tube placement is verified before feeding, and the head of the bed is kept at least 30 degrees to prevent aspiration.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: The nurse assesses an immobile client. Highlight the findings that increase this client's risk for a pressure injury. The client is [[incontinent of urine]], has [[limited mobility]], reports [[good appetite with high protein intake]], has [[poor nutritional intake]], and has [[intact, well-hydrated skin]].

chunks.feedback: Moisture from incontinence increases skin breakdown risk.
Immobility causes prolonged pressure over bony areas.

chunks.text: good appetite with high protein intake
chunks.feedback: Good nutrition is protective, not a risk factor.
Poor nutrition impairs skin integrity and healing.
Healthy skin is protective, not a risk factor.

rationale: Incontinence, immobility, and poor nutrition raise pressure-injury risk; good nutrition and intact skin are protective.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: An immobile client is at risk for complications of immobility. Complete the diagram by selecting the problem, actions to take, and parameters to monitor.

tokens.text: Keep the client flat and still

rationale: Immobility is managed with repositioning and ROM, monitoring skin integrity and joint mobility.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: When a client with left-leg weakness uses a cane, the cane is held in the [1] hand and advances together with the [2] leg.
rationale: The cane is held on the strong (right) side and moves with the weak (left) leg.

subject: Fundamentals of Nursing
stem: Place the steps for giving a client a bed bath in the correct order.
tokens: Wash the arms, chest, and abdomen
